_comment: Cards at the Highsteads (Faces of the Road, MAP-10): a night card for every contract that starts here, and an arrival card for every one that comes back up. Our own text, CC-BY-4.0, credit 'nat20-table contributors'.

cards.text: A painted roadfolk cart stands by the Highsteads wall, kettles clinking on its hooks. The small woman mending a pot by its fire calls over that there is room on her bench, and the boy behind her cannot take his eyes off the Blades' swords.
cards.note: Bel Corrin, halfling roadfolk, and her son Tam. Bel takes no coin: a seat at a roadfolk fire costs a story, because the road is free. Asked for news, she says the men at the Millbeck bridge are nobody's men, only two Highsteads brothers with a debt; she says it as gossip, never as a warning. Ilsa likes them; Bren counts the kettles. Joke: Tam asks the human's character how many dragons they have killed and will not accept none.

choices.text: Ask what news they have of the road.

cards.text: Gwyn the shepherd is waiting at the fold gate when the wagon comes up the last of the track. She has news, and she has been saving it for the Blades.
cards.note: Before the choices, say in one plain sentence what happened at the Millbeck bridge on the way down. Gwyn knew the brothers. If they died (killed_col, killed_dunn), she tells it as news, not blame: the farm below the ridge stands empty, the goblins took the flock and the bridge took the boys, and Rufus's man came up with a paper for the land. If they were spared, Col is back mending the fold. If they fed her dog on the river road (fed_gwyns_dog), she knows who fed it: if it came up with the wagon it runs to her, and if not it came home ahead of them, fat and pleased with itself. Whatever the Blades did for the woman under the ridge, Gwyn has heard it. Joke: she has named a ewe after one of the Blades, and not the one they would guess.

choices.text: Ask about the farm under the ridge.

cards.text: Gwyn the shepherd meets the wagon at the fold gate with a round cheese in a cloth. Col sent it up for the Blades, she says, for speaking up for him at Wendford, and she cuts it for them there at the gate. She has news as well.
cards.note: The card for when the Blades spoke Col out of the stocks at Wendford (col_owes_blades); otherwise gwyn_news. Before the choices, say in one plain sentence what happened at the Millbeck bridge on the way down. Gwyn knew the brothers. Col is back mending the fold, and the cheese is his thanks for the stocks; Gwyn cuts it at the fold gate and it is eaten there, so it never goes on the wagon. If they fed her dog on the river road (fed_gwyns_dog), she knows who fed it: if it came up with the wagon it runs to her, and if not it came home ahead of them, fat and pleased with itself. Whatever the Blades did for the woman under the ridge, Gwyn has heard it. Joke: she has named a ewe after one of the Blades, and not the one they would guess.

choices.text: Ask about the farm under the ridge.
